newsitem.title: USA: Georgia school bond upgrade unlikely to boost debt.
newsitem.headline: Georgia school bond upgrade unlikely to boost debt.

text.p: Despite last week's upgrade from Moody's Investors Service, Georgia school systems that participate in the state's intercept program are less likely than before to issue new bond debt, a state school official told Reuters.

Several of the participating counties have already passed a local option sales tax that allows them to use pay-as-you-go financing instead, said Pat Sandor, a spokesman for the Georgia Department of Education.
"Will it (the upgrade) prompt more issues? The answer is probably not. Instead of a debt basis for funding, they can probably have a revenue basis for funding through the sales tax," Sandor said.
Through the intercept program, the education department intercepts part of the districts' state funding and automatically transfers their debt service payments to paying agents.
"It's almost a certainty, 100 percent guaranteed, that the bonds will be paid," Sandor said.
Moody's upgraded all participating district's bond ratings to Aa3 from A1 last week, citing the program's track record and the state's strong economy.
Georgia school officials did not know exactly how many districts participate in the program but Sandor said the number was small because the application process is cumbersome.

Moody's upgrade affected about $75 million of general obligation bonds issued by seven participating districts -- Banks, Bleckley, Bulloch, Clay, Lumpkin, Newton and Quitman counties, Moody's senior credit officer Maria Matesanz said.
Four of them, Banks, Bleckley, Clay and Lumpkin, approved one-cent sales tax increases to fund school construction on March 18, their first opportunity to do so under a new state law.

The seven countywide districts affected by the Moody's ratings are mainly rural districts that have not been heavy issuers of debt. All seven counties have fewer than 50,000 residents and some fewer than 3,000.
Still, Sandor said, "They're delighted the bond rating has improved. It demonstrates that our systems are being more fiscally responsible and we're pleased with that."
